description: Wire Agent profile -> AgentJob -> AgentSession into a product-level generic AgentSession entry point: launch from an Agent profile, follow-up, and cancel, with runner support for non-workflow session targets and a CLI surface.

tasks.title: Server: AgentJob consumes Agent definition + widen dispatch envelope
tasks.description: Make standalone AgentJob execution consume an Agent definition rather than only a raw prompt. Add `AgentId`, `AgentInstructions`, and `AgentConfig` snapshot fields to `AgentJobInput` (packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Grains/IAgentJobGrain.cs); update `AgentJobGrain.BuildDispatch` to compose Instructions + AgentConfig + prompt into the executed bytes and to populate `ProjectId` + `AgentSessionId` on the dispatch envelope. Widen `WorkDispatch` (IRunnerGrain.cs) with `ProjectId` (string?) and `AgentSessionId` (string?) and propagate both through `RunnerRoutes` into `WorkDispatchResponse` / `RenderedWorkItem`. Workflow dispatch continues to leave the new fields unset. The raw-prompt-only AgentJob path remains supported.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentJobInput carries AgentId, AgentInstructions, AgentConfig snapshot fields populated at launch time
AgentJobGrain.BuildDispatch composes Agent Instructions + AgentConfig + caller prompt into the executed input when an Agent definition is supplied
WorkDispatch carries ProjectId and AgentSessionId; RunnerRoutes propagates them into WorkDispatchResponse so the runner sees authoritative projectId + sessionId for agent jobs
A raw-prompt-only AgentJob (no Agent definition) remains dispatchable and the external agent receives the bare prompt
Workflow dispatch continues to leave ProjectId/AgentSessionId unset and workflow AgentJob behavior is unchanged
Unit tests cover: agent-sourced composition, raw-prompt-only path, and dispatch envelope population (projectId/sessionId set for agent jobs, unset for workflow)
tasks.output: Updated AgentJobInput, AgentJobGrain, IRunnerGrain/WorkDispatch, RunnerRoutes with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D1 (resolve + snapshot at launch) and D4 (plumb projectId/sessionId onto the dispatch envelope). Server-only; safe to deploy before runner changes.

tasks.title: Runner: generalized session target abstraction (prefixed keys + generic connection methods)
tasks.description: Generalize the runner's session identity off the workflowRunId axis so a generic (non-workflow) session is a first-class target. Prefix `AcpSessionManager.key` (packages/runner/src/runtime/acp-connection.ts) as `workflow:{workflowRunId}:{sessionName}` or `generic:{sessionId}`. Make `sessionTargetFromContext` (packages/runner/src/actions/acp/session-events.ts) return the generic shape when OwnerKind = agent-job and a sessionId is present (projectId gate retained). Add new generic `openAgentSession` / `getAgentSession` / `attachAgentSession` / `agentSessionRuntimeEvents` methods to the runner->server connection (packages/runner/src/server/connection.ts) hitting new generic-session URLs; keep existing `*WorkflowAgentSession` methods and URLs byte-identical. Teach the workflow session strategy (packages/runner/src/actions/acp/session-strategies.ts) to take the generic branch (open/attach/runtime-events) when OwnerKind = agent-job + sessionId present instead of falling through to the ephemeral path.
acceptanceCriteria: AcpSessionManager keys are prefixed (workflow: vs generic:) so a workflow session and a generic session never collide on the same in-flight key, even if work ids matched
sessionTargetFromContext returns the generic {projectId, sessionId} shape for agent-job work items carrying a sessionId, and the workflow shape otherwise
New generic *AgentSession connection methods exist and hit distinct URLs from the workflow *WorkflowAgentSession methods
An agent-job work item (no workflowRunId) opens, attaches, and streams runtime events against the generic session identity via the new methods
A workflow work item opens, attaches, and streams runtime events exactly as before (same keys, same URLs, same call sequence)
Unit tests assert: prefixed-key coexistence (no collision), generic vs workflow target derivation, and that generic dispatch routes to the new connection methods while workflow dispatch is unchanged
tasks.output: Updated acp-connection.ts, session-events.ts, connection.ts, session-strategies.ts with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D3 (generalized SessionTarget shape) and D4 (runner consumes projectId/sessionId from the widened envelope). Workflow path must remain bit-compatible.

tasks.title: Server: launch generic AgentSession from an Agent profile (endpoint + session minting)
tasks.description: Add the product launch endpoint `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agents/{agentRef}/sessions` (distinct from the validation-only POST /api/agent-jobs/validate). The handler resolves the Agent in the project via AgentGrain, composes the Agent's Instructions + AgentConfig + the caller's prompt (+ optional context references) into an AgentJobInput snapshot, mints the sessionId up front via `AgentSessionGrain.OpenAsync` with labels `source-kind = agent-launch`, agent id/name, and any context-ref annotations, then submits the AgentJob carrying the minted sessionId, and returns 201 `{ sessionId, agentId, agentName, status }`. Reject empty/whitespace prompt with 400 (no job submitted, no session created) and unknown agent with 404 (no session created). Ensure the AgentJob timeout path transitions a stuck session to a terminal failed state.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agents/{agentRef}/sessions resolves the Agent, composes Instructions + AgentConfig + prompt, executes via a standalone AgentJob that records a generic AgentSession, and returns 201 { sessionId, agentId, agentName, status }
The server mints the sessionId before dispatch (AgentSessionGrain.OpenAsync) and passes it on the AgentJob so the launch response is synchronous and reliable

The resulting AgentSession carries source-kind = agent-launch label plus agent id/name; optional context refs (issue/epic/repository/workspace) are recorded as metadata only and create no scope/mount/supervisor lifecycle
The session is observable through existing session read paths (transcript, runtime events) without a workflowRunId lookup key
Empty/whitespace/missing prompt returns 400 with no AgentJob submitted and no session created
Unknown agentRef returns 404 with no session created
The launch endpoint is distinct from the validation-only /api/agent-jobs/validate route, which remains unchanged
On AgentJob timeout the grain transitions the session to a terminal failed state
Tests cover: successful launch (composition + 201 shape + labels), context-ref recording, empty prompt 400, unknown agent 404, and distinctness from the validation route
tasks.output: New launch endpoint + route registration + session minting wiring with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D1 (server resolves + snapshots at launch) and D2 (server mints sessionId before dispatch). End-to-end observability requires T-002 so runtime events flow back for generic sessions.

tasks.title: Generic AgentSession followup (server endpoint + resolver + SignalR payload + runner handler)
tasks.description: Add `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/followup` (body `{ text }`, non-empty; 200 `{ status: "sent" }` on success) distinct from the issue-scoped followup route which stays unchanged. Add `ResolveGenericFollowupTargetAsync(projectId, sessionId)` to AgentSessionQuerier that loads the AgentSessionGrain by sessionId, reads Runtime.RunnerId + status, and returns a GenericFollowupTarget(runnerId, sessionId, isActive). Generalize the `ReceiveFollowup` SignalR payload to carry a unified `target: SessionTarget` while still populating workflowRunId/sessionName fields for workflow sessions (older runners keep working). On the runner, drop the workflowRunId-non-empty gate in `resolveFollowupTarget` + `handleFollowup` (packages/runner/src/runtime/host.ts, packages/runner/src/server/runner-signalr.ts) and branch on target.kind; for generic targets look up AcpSessionManager by `generic:{sessionId}` and fire-and-forget `connection.prompt()`. Validate: terminal session -> 409, runner offline -> 503, unknown session -> 404, empty text -> 400.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/followup accepts a non-empty text for an active generic session with an online runner and returns 200 { status: "sent" }
Server pushes a ReceiveFollowup SignalR message whose target identifies the generic session (no workflowRunId required); workflow sessions still receive workflowRunId/sessionName fields
Runner resolves the generic target via AcpSessionManager (generic:{sessionId}) and invokes connection.prompt() fire-and-forget without awaiting turn completion
Terminal session (completed/failed/stopped) returns 409; runner offline returns 503; unknown sessionId returns 404; empty/missing text returns 400
The existing issue-scoped POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/{number}/sessions/{name}/followup route and its payload shape remain byte-identical
Runner silently drops a followup for an unknown/unmatched session without throwing
Tests cover server endpoint (all status codes), ResolveGenericFollowupTargetAsync, ReceiveFollowup payload for both shapes, runner handleFollowup branching, and issue-scoped route preservation
tasks.output: New followup endpoint + ResolveGenericFollowupTargetAsync + generalized ReceiveFollowup payload + runner followup branching with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D3 (ReceiveFollowup target generalization) and D5 (split followup-target resolution). Server-side resolver + endpoint can be verified with fakes; runner handler reuses the T-002 key prefix.

tasks.title: Generic AgentSession cancel (server endpoint + CancelAgentSession SignalR + runner handler)
tasks.description: Add `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/cancel` that attempts to cancel the running turn and returns the resulting session state honestly. Add a new server->runner `CancelAgentSession(target: SessionTarget)` SignalR method (distinct from fire-and-forget ReceiveFollowup because cancel needs a reply). The server short-circuits without calling the runner when AgentSessionGrain reports a terminal state. On the runner, handle `CancelAgentSession` by attempting `connection.cancel?(sessionId)` when the ACP connection advertises cancellation, replying with `{ state: "cancelled" | "not-cancellable" | <terminal-state> }`. The HTTP response mirrors the runner's reported state so the API never pretends success. Unknown session -> 404.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/cancel for an active session whose agent supports cancellation attempts to cancel the running turn and returns the resulting session state
When the underlying agent does not support cancellation the response states the session is not currently cancellable and does NOT pretend success
When the session is already terminal (completed/failed/stopped) the server short-circuits and returns the current terminal state without calling the runner
The HTTP response mirrors the runner's reported state (cancelled / not-cancellable / terminal) so the API cannot fake success
Unknown sessionId returns 404
CancelAgentSession is a separate SignalR method from ReceiveFollowup (cancel requires a reply path; followup is fire-and-forget)
Tests cover: cancellable active session, non-cancellable agent reported honestly, terminal short-circuit, unknown session 404, and runner cancel invocation/reply
tasks.output: New cancel endpoint + CancelAgentSession SignalR method + runner cancel handler with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D6. Reuses the SessionTarget shape from T-002 and the session existence from T-003; independent of the followup task (T-004).

tasks.title: CLI: mo agent session launch|followup|cancel subgroup
tasks.description: Add a `session` subgroup under `agent` (packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.Agent.cs) with `launch <agent>`, `followup <sessionId>`, and `cancel <sessionId>` commands. launch sends POST /api/projects/:projectId/agents/:agentId/sessions with the prompt and prints { sessionId, agentId, agentName, status }; followup sends POST /api/projects/:projectId/agent-sessions/:sessionId/followup and prints the delivery status; cancel sends POST /api/projects/:projectId/agent-sessions/:sessionId/cancel and prints the resulting session state. Add a shared read-body-from-flag/file/stdin helper supporting --prompt/--prompt-file/--prompt-stdin (launch) and --text/--text-file/--text-stdin (followup). Reuse ProjectRefOption(), PrintPostAsync / PrintPostWithOutputAsync, and -o table|json. Missing prompt/text fails clearly with exit code 1; server errors (404/409) surface the server message with non-zero exit.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo agent session launch <agent> --prompt <text>` resolves the agent, posts to the launch endpoint, and prints sessionId + agent id/name + status; supports --prompt-file and --prompt-stdin
`mo agent session followup <sessionId> --text <text>` posts to the followup endpoint and prints the delivery status; supports --text-file and --text-stdin
`mo agent session cancel <sessionId>` posts to the cancel endpoint and prints the resulting session state; surfaces not-cancellable and terminal states honestly without reporting success
All three commands accept --project/--project-id and -o table|json; -o json prints the raw server response
Missing --prompt/--text (and no file/stdin equivalent) prints a clear validation error and exits with code 1
Server errors (404 unknown agent/session, 409 terminal) surface the server-provided message with a non-zero exit and no silent success
Tests cover each command's success path, body-source variants (flag/file/stdin), output formats, missing-input validation, and server-error surfacing (using fakes, no real server)
tasks.output: New CLI session subgroup commands + shared body-input helper with tests
tasks.notes: Implements design D7. Placed under `mo agent session` (not top-level `mo session`, not `mo issue session`) because these commands are agent-scoped.
